alicia: Hey perf team — noticed a TTFT jump for route `/api/v1/respond` around 2024-11-20T14:03Z. P50 stayed ~90ms but P95 shot from ~120ms -> ~420ms. Waterfall shows decode CPU stable but kernel attribution tag flipped to `fallback-kernel` for many tokens. Anyone seeing routing or kernel-selector churn?

devin: I saw an autoscaler event at 14:01 and some kernel-selector logs indicating `no-optimised-kernel` for rdx-2l-512q. Suspect prefetch eviction causing more cold KV loads, so kernel falls back to safer (slower) path.

trinh: Can you paste a sample probe run or a small trace? I'll spin up the token sampler against that route.

alicia: Pasting a small snippet from the probe-runner (sanitized):
```
probe_id: pr-9821
route: /api/v1/respond
model: rdx-2l-512q
samples: 120
metrics (ms): ttft_p50=88, ttft_p95=418, decode_p95=110, kernel_fallback_pct=62, kv_hit_pct=71
notes: many tokens attributed to kernel_time="fallback-kernel" in trace tags
```

perfbot: Auto-probe summary for pr-9821 -> anomaly detected: TTL-prefetch misses increased by +28% vs baseline, small-context requests show higher kernel fallback ratio. Related logs: `kernelselector: fallback_reason=kv_eviction` @channel

devin: Thanks. I reran a microprobe with kvcache instrumentation:
```
> ./probe_runner --route /api/v1/respond --model rdx-2l-512q --samples 200 --instrument kvcache,kernel_select
```
Results: mean_kv_miss_per_req=0.34 -> up from 0.09 baseline, fallback_kernel_time median=260ms, optimized_kernel_time median=85ms.

trinh: That lines up. Two hypotheses: 1) microbatch handshake changed after autoscaler up — increased interleaving causes more KV churn; 2) recent kernel selector heuristic (commit 3f7b) prefers safe kernel if prefetch_window < X, but our prefetch_window estimator may be undercounting cold prefixes.

mike: For short-term mitigation can we: a) increase kvcache size for dedicated pool serving that route, or b) tweak selector to prefer opt-kernel when kv_hit_pct > 60? We should also add a per-route TTFT breakdown panel (kernel vs decode vs queue) to the `/api/v1/respond` dashboard.

alicia: Agreed. Quick triage plan:
- trinh: run stratified token sampler (cold vs warm prefixes) + attach kernel-choice traces (ETA 2h)
- devin: roll back selector heuristic commit 3f7b on a canary for that pool and measure (ETA 1h)
- mike: add temporary dashboard panel and alert on kernel_fallback_pct > 30% (ETA 45m)

trinh: Starting sampler now. Running: `./token_sampler --route /api/v1/respond --strata=cold,warm --n=400 --out=gs://perf/ttft-samples/pr-9821`

alicia: Thanks — please paste the trace links here when done. Also tagging @perfbot to post probe diffs after canary. :thumbsup:

perfbot: Canary diff posted -> selector-rollback reduces kernel_fallback_pct from 62% -> 18% on canary nodes; TTFT P95 improved 418ms -> 140ms. Full rollback looks promising but need more samples.

mike: Great signal. After trinh's stratified run we should compute token-level SLI delta and automate a kernel-attribution panel so on future incidents we can quickly see TTFT vs decode vs kernel fallback contribution.

alicia: Assigning follow-up to trinh to make a short runbook note about interpreting token-attribution panels and to mike to update the dashboard. I'll keep the thread updated as canary collects more.

trinh: Got it — will upload a short howto and the sampler results in ~2h.

alicia: Thanks everyone.
